title: Applied Scientist, Navigation
reason: Stack +61; Synergy +10; Entry +15; Exp fit +10; US +10
description_preview:
Description
Amazon is on a mission to redefine the future of automation — and we're looking for exceptional talent to help lead the way. We are building the next generation of advanced robotic systems that seamlessly blend cutting-edge AI, sophisticated control systems, and novel mechanical design to create adaptable, intelligent automation solutions capable of operating safely alongside humans in dynamic, real-world environments.
At Amazon, we leverage the power of machine learning, artificial intelligence, and advanced robotics to solve some of the most complex operational challenges at a scale unlike anywhere else in the world. Our fleet of robots spans hundreds of facilities globally, working in sophisticated coordination to deliver on our promise of customer excellence — and we're just getting started.
As a Scientist in Robot Navigation, you will be at the forefront of this transformation — architecting and delivering navigation systems that are intelligent, safe, and scalable. You will bring deep expertise in learning-based planning and control, a strong understanding of foundation models and their application to embodied agents, and as well as have in-depth understanding of control-theoretic approaches such as model predictive control (MPC)-based trajectory planning. You will develop navigation solutions that seamlessly blend data-driven intelligence with principled control-theoretic guarantees.
Our vision is bold: to build navigation systems that allow robots to move fluidly and safely through dynamic environments — understanding context, anticipating change, and adapting in real time. You will lead research that bridges the gap between cutting-edge academic advances and production grade deployment, collaborating with world-class teams pushing the boundaries of robotic autonomy, manipulation, and human-robot interaction.
Join us in building the next generation of intelligent navigation systems that will define the future of autonomous robotics at scale.
Key job responsibilities
Design, develop, and deploy perception algorithms for robotics systems, including object detection, segmentation, tracking, depth estimation, and scene understanding
Lead research initiatives in computer vision, sensor fusion and 3D perception
Collaborate with cross-functional teams including robotics engineers, software engineers, and product managers to define and deliver perception capabilities
Drive end-to-end ownership of ML models — from data collection and labeling strategy to training, evaluation, and deployment
Mentor junior scientists and engineers; contribute to a culture of technical excellence
Define and track key metrics to measure perception system performance in real-world environments
Publish research findings in top-tier venues (CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, ICRA, NeurIPS, etc.) and contribute to patents
A day in the life
Train ML models for deployment in simulation and real-world robots, identify and document their limitations post-deployment
Drive technical discussions within your team and with key stakeholders to develop innovative solutions to address identified limitations
Actively contribute to brainstorming sessions on adjacent topics, bringing fresh perspectives that help peers grow and succeed — and in doing so, build lasting trust across the team
Mentor team members while maintaining significant hands-on contribution to technical solutions
About The Team
Our team is a group is a diverse group of scientists and engineers passionate about building intelligent machines. We value curiosity, rigor, and a bias for action. We believe in learning from failure and iterating quickly toward solutions that matter.
Basic Qualifications
Experience programming in Java, C++, Python or related language
PhD in Robotics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Controls, or a related field
2+ years of experience in robot navigation, motion planning, or autonomous systems
Deep expertise in learning-based approaches to navigation (e.g., imitation learning, reinforcement learning, neural motion planning, diffusion-based policies)
Strong experience with Model Predictive Control (MPC) and optimization-based planning (PyTorch, JAX, or equivalent)
Proven track record of translating research into deployed systems
Preferred Qualifications
Experience applying foundation models or large pre-trained models to robotics tasks (navigation, manipulation, or embodied AI)
Familiarity with world models, visual navigation, or vision-languageaction models
Experience with sim-to-real transfer and high-fidelity simulation environments (Isaac Sim, MuJoCo, Gazebo)
Knowledge of SLAM, localization, and mapping systems
Experience with ROS/ROS2 and real-time robotics middleware
Hands-on experience deploying navigation systems on physical robots in dynamic, real-world environments
Experience with safety-critical systems and formal verification of learned controllers
Familiarity with multi-agent coordination and fleet-level navigation

description_preview:
At Lance, Product Engineers own products end to end.
We don’t separate product into people who decide what to build, people who design it, and people who implement it. We believe the best products are built when the same person deeply understands the problem, makes the product decisions, builds the solution, and learns from how customers actually use it.
A Product Engineer at Lance owns the full 0 → 1 cycle.
The four cycles
1. Discover
Understand the problem firsthand. Talk to customers, spend time in hotels, watch how people work, and figure out what actually needs to be solved.
2. Design
Turn that understanding into a product. Decide how it should work, prototype the experience, make tradeoffs, and define what the first version should be.
3. Build
Ship it. Own the technical decisions, write the code, integrate the systems, and take the product all the way to production.
4. Iterate
Put it in customers' hands. Watch what works and what breaks, measure usage, talk to users, and keep improving it until it becomes something people depend on.
You do all four.
There is no handoff from PM → designer → engineer. You are responsible for taking an ambiguous problem and turning it into a product that works in the real world.
What you'll do
Own new products from 0 → 1
Spend time with hotel teams and identify problems worth solving
Prototype and ship new AI-native product experiences
Make product, design, and engineering decisions
Build across the stack when necessary
Deploy your work directly into real hotels
Talk to users and observe how they actually use what you built
Iterate quickly based on real-world feedback
Own the quality and outcome of the product, not just the code
What we're looking for
We care much more about what you can build than the number of years you've been an engineer.
You’ll probably thrive here if you:
Have exceptional product judgment
Can turn ambiguity into something concrete
Move extremely quickly without sacrificing quality
Care about design and user experience
Are comfortable working across the stack
Want ownership rather than a narrowly defined engineering task
Talk to customers instead of guessing what they want
Have built things from scratch before
Treat shipping as the beginning of the product cycle, not the end
How we think about the role
At Lance, we give you a problem.
Your job is to understand it deeply enough to figure out what should exist, then make it exist.

Job Description
Primary Function of Position
As a Staff Software Engineer reporting to the Managing Staff Software Engineer in the MP Platform Engineering group, you will be the technical leader responsible for the architecture and implementation of mixed-criticality embedded virtualization. You’ll define how a next-generation surgical robotic system safely consolidates critical/real-time and non-critical software onto shared hardware. You will own the key elements of the virtualization safety strategy: partitioning architecture, hypervisor configuration, silicon and platform software tuning for freedom from interference.
Beyond virtualization, you will leverage your broad expertise and unique technical knowledge to contribute to company objectives, lead cross-functional projects from concept through completion, and coach colleagues in advancing their technical expertise. You will take ownership of multiple aspects of the embedded platform, exercising independent judgment on ambiguous, high-impact problems and influencing senior stakeholders on technical direction and associated risk.

Ramp on the platform's hardware/software stack, safety requirements, and existing hypervisor deployments.
Deliver an architecture recommendation for the hypervisor strategy, accounting for partitioning, determinism, and the safety implications of each hypervisor's certification posture.
Characterize behavior on target hardware and produce the initial analysis artifacts demonstrating freedom from interference.
Stand up the instrumentation needed to give the team visibility into timing, utilization, and VM/platform health.
Essential Job Duties
Define the virtualization safety architecture for a mixed-criticality system, ensuring spatial and temporal isolation between safety-critical and non-safety-critical applications.
Prototype and evaluate Xen and QNX hypervisors, defining an architecture based on safety, determinism, certifiability, and platform fit.
Own hypervisor system configuration and integration, implementing creative solutions to overcome platform limitations and gaps in vendor support.
Architect and implement deterministic inter-VM communication and device virtualization using virtio, shared memory, and PCIe/other device passthrough.
Plan and execute the analysis and verification needed to demonstrate freedom from interference, deterministic timing, and safe failure behavior in a regulated environment.
Lead failure modes and effects analysis for the virtualized platform, translating identified failures and technology limitations into design mitigations, fault containment, and defined recovery or degraded behaviors.
Build platform observability that exposes guest and hypervisor health, resource utilization, latency, jitter, and other relevant system health signals on target hardware

Demonstrated expertise in designing scalable, high-performance embedded software architectures; advanced proficiency in modern C++ and Python for real-time systems.

Extensive experience in Linux/QNX environments, including kernel modules, resource managers, POSIX applications, and distributed inter-processor communication frameworks.
Proven expertise with FPGAs, hardware accelerators, PCIe transport/configuration/enumeration concepts, and network stacks; strong ability to root-cause interdependent hardware/software problems.
Proven track record of leading strategic technical initiatives from concept through completion; ability to work independently and drive results with limited supervision.
Exceptional communication skills with demonstrated ability to articulate complex technical concepts and influence senior leadership across organizational levels.
Strong leadership capabilities, including mentoring engineers at all levels, providing technical direction, and potentially supervising activities of others.
Required Education And Training
Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related engineering discipline.
Minimum of 12 years of related experience with a Bachelor's degree; or 8 years with a Master's degree; or a PhD with 5 years of experience.
Preferred Skills And Experience
Experience with Xen internals (dom0/domU, PV/HVM/PVH, xl configuration, Xen on ARM or x86) or with hypervisor contributions upstream.
Experience with functional safety and regulatory standards such as ISO 26262, IEC 61508, DO-178C/DO-297, IEC 62304, ISO 14971, or IEC 60601, including partitioning and interference requirements.

Collaborate with our Data/ML and Content Pipeline teams to build new features and make improvements to our document ingestion infrastructure

Collaborate with Design and PM
Contribute to a shared design system
Make contributions to improving our frontend infrastructure

About the role:
Join our FDE team and work directly with some of the world's largest organizations to turn their most ambitious ideas into production applications on Replit. As a Forward Deployed Engineer, you'll partner closely with customers to understand their technical and business needs, architect solutions, and build the integrations and applications required to deploy Replit successfully within complex enterprise environments.

Bridge Customers and Product: Develop a deep understanding of how enterprises use Replit and translate field insights, technical constraints, and recurring customer needs into actionable feedback for Replit’s product and engineering teams.

Experience designing and owning complex technical systems from architecture through production

About Us
The first baby boomers turn 80 this year. Over the next decade, the population most likely to need daily care will grow faster than the buildings, the staff, or the systems available to serve it.
Sage is the care intelligence platform for senior living and skilled nursing. We connect the hardware senior care runs on, including nurse call, fall management, and wander management, with software caregivers actually use. That consistent use is what produces reliable data, and reliable data is what gives operators a true picture of how their communities are running.
Sage is a collaborative team of ambitious, multi-disciplinary entrepreneurs on a mission to reinvent senior care with a modern operating system for caregivers. Millions of people depend on this care getting better, and we move with the urgency that deserves.
About This Role
Somewhere in a senior living community right now, a camera and a small computer are working together to figure out whether the person who just fell is okay. The community's network connection may be fiddly and unreliable, and the deployed hardware has its own quirks. That system is one of thousands just like it, running software your team wrote, doing work that matters if something goes wrong.
This is the job: building and evolving the systems that enable edge hardware (including cameras and other sensors), and cloud infrastructure to work together reliably, at scale, even when a connection drops or a device behaves in a way nobody planned for.
If you've spent real time in Linux, networking, or hardware because you were curious rather than because a job required it, we think you could thrive in this role. We care less about whether you've used our exact stack before and more about whether you're the kind of engineer who takes a system apart, mentally or literally, until you understand why it works.
You'll define the architecture for Sage's edge computing platform, own hard and often unsolved problems (e.g. fall detection, resident location tracking, integrating unpredictable third-party hardware), and help set the technical bar for the engineering org. You'll also mentor other engineers and be a voice in how we build, not just what we build.
What You'll Do
Shape the architecture of a fleet of edge devices deployed in the physical world, and the cloud systems that orchestrate, monitor, and update them
Dig into ambiguous, often novel problems (resident location modeling, fall detection, sensor fusion)
Build the diagnostic tooling that lets us understand what's happening on hardware we can't just walk up to
Get hands-on with remote troubleshooting when something breaks in the field, reasoning about network, hardware, and software all at once
Work directly with other Sage teams to ship solutions end to end collaboratively
Review code and run design discussions, and help less experienced engineers get better by through teaching and explaining
Push back on us when there's a better way to build something; we'd rather be right than consistent
What We're Looking For
This describes the kind of engineer who tends to thrive in this role. If most of it sounds like you, we want to hear from you, even if your resume doesn't map cleanly onto "IoT engineer."
You have professional experience working in complex backend systems:
This usually means at least 7+ years of work experience, building (and sometimes breaking) within systems that grew and changed over time.
You understand systems, not just frameworks:
You're comfortable in Linux/Unix environments well past the level of running commands you looked up. You've broken things, debugged them, and come out the other side understanding what happened.
You have real depth in at least one language
(object-oriented or otherwise; Java, C++, Rust, Go, Python, and C# are all fine signals) with strong computing fundamentals and can reason about memory, concurrency, and performance at a lower level.
You have working knowledge of networking
, enough to reason about what happens when a device drops offline mid-update, or why a connection is behaving strangely, without needing to look up the fundamentals first.
You're demonstrably curious,
e.g. in side projects, open source contributions, a home lab, a technical hobby, or a history of teaching yourself things. We care less about the domain than that it exists.
You can hold complexity and still ship.
You've led a technical effort, official title or not, from a fuzzy problem to a real outcome, and you know how to make tradeoffs under ambiguity.
Re: years of experience:
we're not fixated on the number. We care about depth and range. Someone with 6 years of genuinely varied, hands-on systems work will often be a stronger fit than someone with 10 years in a narrow web stack. If you're unsure whether your background counts, apply anyway and let us figure that out together.

Experience designing across edge and cloud environments, including OTA updates and fleet management

description_preview:
At Lance, Members of Technical Staff are engineers who can own hard problems end to end.
We don’t hire people into narrow boxes like frontend engineer, backend engineer, or AI engineer. The problems we’re solving cut across product, AI, infrastructure, systems, and the physical world. We want engineers who are comfortable going wherever the problem takes them.
You might spend one week building an AI agent, the next designing the infrastructure behind it, and the next shipping a product used by hotel employees every day.
Your responsibility is not a specific layer of the stack. Your responsibility is making the system work.
What you'll do
Build and own major products and technical systems from 0 → 1
Develop AI agents that can reason, take actions, and operate reliably in the real world
Work across frontend, backend, infrastructure, models, data, and integrations
Build agent harnesses, evals, context systems, and learning loops
Design systems that coordinate humans and AI agents
Integrate with legacy hotel systems and turn messy real-world workflows into reliable software
Prototype new interfaces across voice, mobile, desktop, and hardware
Deploy directly into hotels and learn from how the systems behave in production
Debug problems across the entire stack
Make foundational technical decisions that shape the future of Lance
What we're looking for
We care less about your title or years of experience and more about your ability to solve difficult problems.
You’ll likely thrive here if you:
Are an exceptional engineer with strong technical fundamentals
Can move between product engineering and AI engineering
Have built complex systems from scratch
Are comfortable operating with very little structure
Learn new technologies extremely quickly
Care deeply about reliability and product quality
Can reason from first principles instead of reaching for the standard solution
Want ownership over outcomes, not tickets
Are excited by problems where the answer is not obvious
How we work
There is no clean boundary between AI engineering, product engineering, and infrastructure here.
If an AI agent is failing, you might change the prompt, redesign the eval, modify the architecture, rebuild the workflow, or change the product itself.
We expect engineers to understand the entire system well enough to make that call.
At Lance, the best engineers don't just implement the future.
They figure out what needs to be invented, then build it.

AI Engineering and Delivery is the customer-obsessed engineering group building the agentic AI and enterprise-scale search systems that power Now Assist, AI Agents, and the AI-driven experiences our customers rely on every day. We build AI as foundational platform infrastructure — prioritizing robustness, performance, safety, and real-world customer impact at scale.

Emerging tech is a small senior group inside AI Engineering and Delivery. We turn early bets on AI and emerging tech into strategic capability for our customers, our people, and ServiceNow. Trust, safety, and governance. Own the guardrails: observability, human-in-the-loop controls, and compliance infrastructure that make autonomous systems safe to deploy at scale.
Retrieval and grounding. Work closely with our search team to ensure agents are grounded in accurate, low-latency retrieval — RAG pipelines, hybrid search, re-ranking, and evaluation — as a critical dependency of agentic quality.

Technical leadership and strong bias for action. Set the architectural patterns the group works from. Own the hard design calls, run the design reviews, and raise the bar on agentic design and production AI discipline across engineers and principals.

Work on emerging model capabilities and applying them to real world customer problems on a short timeline

9+ years of software engineering with strong fundamentals in data structures, algorithms, and distributed systems.

Production-grade Python. Systems language (Go, Java, or C++) is a plus.
Working experience with frontier AI SDKs (Anthropic, Google, or OpenAI) — prompt engineering, structured outputs, and model evaluation in production settings.
Familiarity with RAG and retrieval patterns in production — vector stores, hybrid search, and retrieval evaluation metrics.
Track record of technical leadership: architecture ownership, code quality bar-raising, and mentoring engineers on production AI practices.

Published work or open-source contributions in agentic systems or retrieval.
Exposure to LLM fine-tuning or inference optimization in production

AI Control Tower with kill-switch capabilities and cross-vendor agent governance. These are production systems at Fortune 500 scale, not roadmap slides.

Senior AI Engineer – Edge Dialog Systems
BrightAI is a high-growth Physical AI company transforming how businesses interact with the physical world through intelligent automation. Our AI platform processes visual, spatial, and temporal data from billions of real-world events—captured across edge devices, mobile sensors, and cloud infrastructure—to enable intelligent decision-making at scale.
We are now hiring a
Sr. AI Engineer – Edge Dialog Systems
to own and evolve the on-device conversational AI that powers our industrial safety wearable. The assistant guides field technicians through safety-critical procedures by voice, and it runs on the device itself, under hard latency, memory, and thermal budgets, with deterministic safeguards that take precedence over model output.
This is a systems role rather than a prompt-and-retrieve role. The competencies of a strong LLM and RAG engineer are needed for the position, but the work itself is dialog systems engineering at the edge, where most conversational turns are resolved by deterministic and embedding-based methods, and the language model is the last resort rather than the first move.
You will work at the intersection of natural language understanding (NLU), small language models (SLM), and embedded software, building a system in which a wrong answer is a safety concern and not merely a quality issue.
Responsibilities
Own the on-device dialog pipeline end to end: intent routing, hybrid intent classification (pattern matching combined with embedding similarity and out-of-domain detection), text normalization for noisy speech input, and the multi-step guided-procedure engine.
Maintain and extend the deterministic safety layer that wraps the language model—confirmation and echo-back gating, criticality tagging, negation handling—so that a misheard answer on a safety-critical step cannot pass silently.
Run SLM inference on-device under memory, computational complexity, and latency budgets, and reduce the per-turn inference cost through model selection, quantization, and runtime optimization.
Preserve and extend the zero-shot configuration model, in which new device commands and customer procedures are authored as data rather than released as code, so that a new customer can be onboarded in hours rather than weeks.
Coordinate the device deployment pipeline with the edge team
Maintain the API contract with on-device voice pipeline & its speech-to-text (STT) stack.
Define and run on-device benchmarks: latency, accuracy, and false-accept/reject rates on safety-critical steps; use measurements to drive engineering decisions.
Build and maintain golden datasets and a non-regression suite, and use them as the release gate as the command and procedure catalogs grow.
Lead the migration from zero-shot to fine-tuned on-device models in order to reduce latency, without reintroducing a per-customer retraining burden.
Collaborate with product, firmware, and cloud teams, and bring new capabilities online, including additional languages, device commands, and guided workflows.

Trained in AI, Machine Learning, Electrical/Computer Engineering, or a related field, with specialization in NLP, speech, or deep learning; or equivalent industry experience delivering production conversational AI systems.

LLM and retrieval foundation — the baseline for this role
5+ years of experience in ML/AI, with a strong focus on NLP, LLMs, or conversational AI.
Strong applied experience with LLMs: prompting, structured output, tool and function calling, evaluation, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) – together with the judgment to recognize when a model should not be used at all.
Solid command of embeddings and semantic similarity (e.g., cosine similarity, centroid versus maximum-similarity strategies, threshold tuning, and out-of-domain detection).

Strong experience building edge conversational systems, including multi-turn dialog/state management and efficient intent/NLU pipelines using local-first, cheap-to-expensive inference strategies.
Disambiguation and repair: resolving ambiguous intent and noisy spoken references, and asking a clarifying question or re-prompting rather than committing to a confident wrong answer.

This is a job that Jill, our AI Recruiter, is recruiting for on behalf of one of our customers.
She will pick the best candidates from Jack's network.
The next step is to speak to Jack.
Job Title
Founding Engineer
Salary
Not Disclosed
Company Description
Futurelovers.com is a seed-stage San Francisco startup building Hivemind, an AI-native social intelligence product backed by First Round Capital and founders of Twitter, Shopify, and Pinterest. The team, composed of ex-Apple and ex-Midjourney talent, is creating a frontier platform that allows AI to reason across networks of human relationships.
Job Description
As the first full-time engineer at Futurelovers.com, you will co-own the technical foundation of Hivemind from day zero. You will architect core infrastructure for AI-driven social reasoning, bridging the gap between distributed systems and human networks. Working alongside elite design and research talent, you’ll define a new category at the intersection of AI and collective coordination.
Location
San Francisco, USA
Why this role is remarkable
Join as a founding technical member, shaping the product direction and research alongside a world-class team from Apple and Midjourney.
Build on an elite foundation backed by First Round Capital and visionary angels like Biz Stone (Twitter) and Tobi Lütke (Shopify).
Invent original systems for collective intelligence that don't yet exist, solving frontier problems in how AI reasons across human relationship networks.
What You Will Do
Architect core infrastructure for context management and model orchestration to enable AI reasoning across complex, fractal networks of human relationships.
Build and scale real-time learning systems that continuously integrate feedback from many users to evolve social narratives.
Own the entire technical stack from backend to AI infrastructure, moving from high-level vision to production-ready code in days.
The ideal candidate
Possesses production experience shipping and scaling robust distributed systems or AI infrastructure, with a mastery of backend technologies.
Demonstrates a founder mindset with the ability to own large, ambiguous problems end-to-end rather than just executing predefined specifications.
Brings experience building social products or a deep understanding of network effects to create technology that enhances human coordination.
Who are Jack & Jill?
Ok, I'll go first. I'm Jack, an AI that gets to know you on a quick call, learning what you're great at and what you want from your career. Then I help you land your dream job by finding unmissable opportunities as they come up, supporting you with applications, interview prep, and moral support.
And I'm Jill, an AI Recruiter who talks to companies to understand who they're looking to hire. Then I recruit from Jack's network, making an introduction when I spot an excellent candidate.
How does this work?
Jack's an AI agent for job searching and career coaching. He works for you.
Jill is the AI recruiter working for the company. She recruits from Jack's network.
If it's a match and the company wants to meet you, they'll make the intro. In the meantime, if you'd like, Jack will send you excellent alternatives.
We never post fake jobs
This isn't a trick. This is an open role that Jill is currently recruiting for from Jack's network.
Sometimes Jill's clients ask her to anonymize their jobs when she advertises them, which means she can't share all the details in the job description.
We appreciate this can make them look a bit suspect, but there isn't much we can do about it.
Give Jack a spin! You could land this role. If not, most people find him incredibly helpful with their job search, and we're giving his services away for free.

Design, build, train, evaluate, deploy, and own ML models in production that improve transaction categorization, risk scoring, and data enrichment across Financial Connections
Design and build large-scale ML systems that operate on diverse financial data from thousands of institutions
Experiment and iterate on ML models (using tools such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, XGBoost) to achieve key business goals around data quality and accuracy
Develop pipelines and automated processes to train and evaluate models in offline and online environments
Integrate ML models into production systems and ensure their scalability and reliability
Collaborate with product, data science, and engineering partners across Stripe to identify opportunities where ML can improve outcomes for merchants and consumers
Engage with the latest ML/AI developments and take calculated risks in transforming innovative ideas into productionized solutions
Mentor engineers and contribute to a strong ML engineering culture within the team

10+ years of industry experience building and shipping ML systems in production
Proficient with ML libraries and frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, XGBoost, as well as Spark
Hands-on experience in designing, training, and evaluating machine learning models

MS or PhD degree in ML/AI or a related field (e.g., math, physics, statistics, computer science)
Experience in fintech, open banking, or financial data domains
Experience with NLP, LLMs, or text classification at scale
Experience in adversarial or noisy-data domains such as fraud detection, risk modeling, or data quality

Early-stage robotics infrastructure startup

This role is central to building the data engine for next-generation intelligent machines.

San Francisco, USA

Founding-level ownership of the core data infrastructure used to train advanced robotic models.

Build and maintain robust ETL pipelines for synchronizing video, sensor, and robot state data.

Join our
AI & Engineering
team in transforming technology platforms, driving innovation, and helping make a significant impact on our clients' success. AI & Engineering
leverages cutting-edge engineering capabilities to build, deploy, and operate integrated/verticalized sector solutions in software, data, AI, network, and hybrid cloud infrastructure. Work you'll do
As an
AI and Data Science Engineer III
on the AI & Data team, you will be responsible for driving technology-focused client delivery across complex engagements.
Manage day-to-day interactions with client stakeholders and sponsors, acting as the primary technical point of contact for your workstream
Design and build Generative AI and agentic solutions using Claude, including agent orchestration, tool integration, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) based integrations, using the Claude Agent SDK and Claude Cowork
Manage and deliver components of client engagements spanning solution design, prototyping, testing, and production rollout

Identify risks, assumptions, and constraints early, and implement approved mitigations to protect delivery

Designing and building agentic AI solutions powered by Claude, from proof-of-concept through production deployment
Implementing multi-agent systems that automate business processes, integrate with enterprise tools, and operate within defined autonomy and guardrails
Modernizing existing AI/ML or data platforms to incorporate Generative AI capabilities, including retrieval-augmented generation and agent-based orchestration
Advising clients on Generative AI adoption strategy, responsible AI practices, and model/platform selection
Partnering directly with client technology, data, and business stakeholders to scope and deliver AI solutions
A successful candidate would possess these skills:
Ability to work independently and collaborate as part of a team
Effective written and verbal communication skills
Meticulous attention to detail and quality of work product
Ability to build and sustain professional relationships
Ability to lead projects or workstreams
Ability to manage and prioritize multiple tasks in a fast-paced and dynamic environment
Strong interpersonal skills and professional demeanor
Ability to meet deadlines
Ability to provide clear guidance to others
The team
Our
AI & Data
practice offers comprehensive solutions for designing, developing, and operating advanced Data and AI platforms, products, insights, and services. We help clients innovate, enhance, and manage their data, AI, and analytics capabilities, ensuring they can grow and scale effectively.
Qualifications
Required:
4+ years of experience designing, developing, and delivering production AI/ML solutions, including at least 1 year delivering production Generative AI or Agentic AI systems
2+ years of hands-on experience developing AI/ML applications in Python
At least 1 year of direct experience designing or implementing production agentic workflows involving capabilities such as orchestration, tool integration, state management, evaluation, guardrails, and human-in-the-loop controls
At least 1 year of hands-on experience developing agentic AI solutions using the Claude Agent SDK, including agent orchestration, tool integration, permissions, or MCP integrations
At least 1 year of hands-on experience developing and deploying production solutions using Anthropic Claude models through the native Anthropic API or a supported cloud platform
At least 1 year of experience applying prompt engineering, context engineering, structured outputs, and related techniques to improve the performance, reliability, and usability of AI solutions
1+ years of experience leading project workstreams or engagements, translating business problems into AI solutions, and delivering measurable outcomes
Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science, AI, or a related field

Experience in consulting or other client-facing delivery roles
Experience using Claude Cowork to support enterprise workflows, automation, research, or other knowledge-work use cases

title: Member of Technical Staff ($150k-$300k + Equity) at Series B backed frontier AI lab
reason: Blocked company: Jack & Jill
reject_reason: Blocked company: Jack & Jill
description_preview:
This is a job that Jill, our AI Recruiter, is recruiting for on behalf of one of our customers.
She will pick the best candidates from Jack's network.
The next step is to speak to Jack.
Job Title
Member of Technical Staff - Senior Software Engineer
Salary
$150k-$300k + Equity
Company Description
Series B backed frontier AI lab
Job Description
Join a high-velocity team of researchers and engineers building critical infrastructure for the next generation of human-aligned AI. You will develop complex RL environments, robust backend services, and sophisticated tooling to stress-test frontier models. This role offers the chance to define architecture and drive execution at the cutting edge of AI safety.
Location
San Francisco, USA
Why this role is remarkable
Work alongside a world-class engineering team with experience from top-tier research labs like Meta AI, Amazon AGI, and Google.
Direct impact on the safety and alignment of future AGI systems through foundational simulation research and evaluation infrastructure.
High-autonomy environment at a well-funded, Series B startup during a period of rapid team expansion and technical growth.
What You Will Do
Build end-to-end RL environments for training and evaluating AI agents using React, TypeScript, Python, and FastAPI.
Develop shared tooling and infrastructure for trajectory review, reward hacking checks, and environment QA across multiple platforms.
Partner with Applied Researchers to translate complex environment designs into robust, production-grade software and evaluation systems.
The ideal candidate
Has 4+ years of experience building production software with a full-stack background in React/TypeScript and Python or Go.
Demonstrated experience working with LLM APIs, tool calling, and agentic loops to build custom integrations or developer tools.
Proven track record of owning complex systems end-to-end within a high-velocity startup or small, high-impact engineering team.
Who are Jack & Jill?
Ok, I'll go first. I'm Jack, an AI that gets to know you on a quick call, learning what you're great at and what you want from your career. Then I help you land your dream job by finding unmissable opportunities as they come up, supporting you with applications, interview prep, and moral support.
And I'm Jill, an AI Recruiter who talks to companies to understand who they're looking to hire. Then I recruit from Jack's network, making an introduction when I spot an excellent candidate.
How does this work?
Jack's an AI agent for job searching and career coaching. He works for you.
Jill is the AI recruiter working for the company. She recruits from Jack's network.
If it's a match and the company wants to meet you, they'll make the intro. In the meantime, if you'd like, Jack will send you excellent alternatives.
We never post fake jobs
This isn't a trick. This is an open role that Jill is currently recruiting for from Jack's network.
Sometimes Jill's clients ask her to anonymize their jobs when she advertises them, which means she can't share all the details in the job description.
We appreciate this can make them look a bit suspect, but there isn't much we can do about it.
Give Jack a spin! You could land this role. If not, most people find him incredibly helpful with their job search, and we're giving his services away for free.

Uber AI Solutions (UAIS) is a startup inside Uber, building the data and evaluation infrastructure behind the next generation of AI. The models making headlines are only as good as the data and feedback they learn from, and that is the work we do.
We are an agile team moving at startup speed with the full weight of Uber behind us: global reach, world class infrastructure, and one of the largest human networks in the world. We pair that network with machine learning to produce the high quality, model ready data that the most advanced AI teams on earth depend on. Our work spans every modality, from text, images, and video to audio and physical AI and AVs, and reaches across dozens of countries.
This is a place for builders who want real ownership. Here you own a problem, not a ticket: you take a vertical from start to finish, the machine learning, the backend systems, and the product, and drive it from a blank page to something the best customers in AI rely on every day. You work shoulder to shoulder with product managers and other exceptional engineers, go as deep as the problem demands, and make the calls that decide whether your area wins. It is the closest thing to running your own company, with a rocket strapped to it.
If you want your work to show up in the AI systems shaping the world, and you want to build it like a founder, this is the team.

Build the ML and backend systems that make the growth real and durable, going deep on the hardest problems yourself.
Own your vertical end to end: set the direction, find where the growth is, and drive the business metrics that matter, such as revenue, customers, and market reach.
Move fast and decisively in ambiguity, making the strategic and technical calls that decide whether the business wins.
Be a trusted technical partner in the most important customer relationships, using them to grow the account and shape what you build next.
Build the team and raise the bar so the business can keep scaling.

Master's or PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Electrical Engineering, Mathematics, or a related discipline.
7+ years building and shipping products powered by ML, with a history of owning both the technology and the business results for a significant product area.

Deep expertise in both machine learning systems and backend distributed systems, with the ability to build production systems that scale as the business grows.
A track record of finding the highest leverage opportunities in an ambiguous space and driving them to real business impact.
Exceptional communication and leadership skills, with the ability to align customers, product, and business leadership around a growth agenda.
